resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR says the first structure was built in 1936; firelookout.com says the site was developed in 1933. The brief's 1936 is the NHLR date. The story gives both dates and does not pick one.

The NHLR says the tower is staffed as needed (undated). Firelookout.com (undated) says it is presently deemed unsafe to occupy. The Aug 2023 forest notice does not name Black Butte among its staffed towers. The story reports all three and does not claim a current staffing status.

sources.title: Malheur National Forest staffs fire lookouts

notes_for_editor: Only three sources. The NHLR and firelookout.com pages are both undated, so current status and staffing are unverified. Build year conflicts (1936 NHLR, 1933 firelookout.com). Brief design L-4 and height 6.1 m match the NHLR's 20-ft pole tower; the 20-ft figure is read as the tower height. Searches mostly returned the Black Butte near Sisters (Deschutes NF, Jefferson County, 1934/1995 towers) and a 2021 Black Butte Fire 8 miles NE of Antelope Lookout; neither is this tower and neither was used. Access is provisional. Editor should check with the Prairie City Ranger District on current status before publishing. No photos added.
